BXL-2425-00013-v13.headline: Cancel every Brussels licence for the export or transit of weapons (and dual-use goods) to Israel, and have the Region press the federal government to back the World Court's Gaza genocide case, oppose any forced expulsion of Gazans, and push for sanctions.
BXL-2425-00013-v13.proposed_by: PTB, PS, Ecolo, Groen, Vooruit.brussels, Team Fouad Ahidar (El Mokadem, Ikazban, Tahar, Groothedde, Busselen, Mouani, De Smedt, El Yousfi, Parga Vega, Khattabi — replacing Emmery)
BXL-2425-00013-v13.source_brief:
A ceasefire took hold in Gaza on 19 January 2025, but the proposers call it fragile. This resolution turns the Brussels Region's own levers and its weight as Europe's capital toward the conflict: cancel every regional licence to export or move weapons and dual-use technology where military use can't be ruled out, and push the federal government to reaffirm Belgium's support for the genocide case at the International Court of Justice, oppose Trump's announced plan to expel Gaza's population, and plead for sanctions against those responsible for the bloodshed. The text was reworked in session with a long string of amendments.

- **The Region's direct lever** — end the export or transit of arms and of dual-use goods to Israel when it can't be certain they won't be used militarily; this is the part Brussels can act on itself.
- **What it asks the federal level** — reaffirm support for the ICJ genocide proceedings, oppose forced displacement of Gazans, summon the US and Israeli ambassadors, and plead in Belgium and the EU for sanctions against the political and military leaders responsible.
- **It cuts both ways** — the same text condemns Hamas's 7 October attacks as terrorist acts and demands the release of the remaining hostages, alongside its condemnation of Israel's conduct.
- **The rub:** is a regional parliament right to wield its arms-licensing power and its diplomatic voice to take a hard line on Gaza — or does a Brussels resolution on a federal foreign-policy matter, leaning heavily on one side of a contested war, import the conflict into local politics without changing facts on the ground?
BXL-2425-00013-v13.deep_facts:
- The base text (the committee's text, then amended in plenary) seeks an immediate/permanent ceasefire in Gaza and measures against Israel; the proposers frame the Region as able to act through its own powers as 'capital of Europe' (CRI, 14 Feb 2025; doc A-16).
- Direct regional lever (amendment n° 3): in response to a UN General Assembly resolution, cancel all licences for the export or transit of weapons and their technologies — whether for military or civilian use — and of dual-use goods and technologies where it cannot be established with certainty that they cannot be used for military purposes (CRI, 14 Feb 2025; am. n° 3, A-16).
- Operative asks to the Brussels Government and (via it) the federal government include: ask the federal government to reaffirm support for the proceedings before the International Court of Justice on the allegations of genocide in Gaza; use all the Region's own powers to prevent further escalation; invite the federal government to work within the EU for peace and a negotiated two-State solution; mobilise additional humanitarian resources; plead within Belgium and the EU for sanctions against the political and military leaders responsible for the bloodshed in Gaza and Lebanon; insist on the release of the remaining Israeli hostages; maintain sanctions against Hezbollah and Hamas (CRI, 14 Feb 2025; A-16).
- Amendments tabled in plenary added: authorising the dispatch of independent investigators to Gaza to establish whether the acts constitute genocide under Article II of the Genocide Convention (am. n° 6); recognising, per the ICJ order of 26 January 2024, the plausible risk of genocide in Gaza (am. n° 7); recognising and supporting that ICJ order (am. n° 8); supporting the actions of the ICJ and the International Criminal Court and calling on the federal State to execute their decisions (am. n° 9); categorically opposing US President Donald Trump's announced plan to forcibly expel the Palestinian population from Gaza, taking all legal and diplomatic measures and envisaging sanctions (am. n° 10); summoning the US ambassador over Trump's plan and the Israeli ambassador for violating the ceasefire (am. n° 11) (CRI, 14 Feb 2025; A-16).
- The text also condemns Hamas's violence against civilians as terrorist acts and flagrant violations of international law, and condemns the disproportionate use of force by Israel in Gaza as possibly amounting to war crimes (CRI, 14 Feb 2025; A-16).
- Cited figures (stated, attributed to UN/speakers): more than 47,000 dead in the Gaza Strip including nearly 15,000 children, and close to 4,000 dead in Lebanon (UN figures cited); 1.9 million people in Gaza displaced repeatedly and 1.3 million in Lebanon and Israel; 95% of schools destroyed; UN had at that stage only 3.6% of the estimated funding needed for the first 42-day ceasefire phase; in the West Bank since 7 October 2023, 806 Palestinians killed and 7,138 injured (CRI, 14 Feb 2025; A-16).
- Legal/diplomatic references (not enacted by this text): ICC arrest warrants of 21 November 2024 against Israeli PM Benjamin Netanyahu and former defence minister Yoav Gallant for war crimes and crimes against humanity in Gaza between 8 October 2023 and 20 May 2024; the Israel–Hamas ceasefire concluded 15 January 2025 (three phases) and entered into force 19 January 2025; the Israel–Hezbollah ceasefire of 27 November 2024; a US presidential decree of 4 February 2025 announcing US withdrawal from the UN Human Rights Council (CRI, 14 Feb 2025; A-16).
- The resolution decides to transmit the text to the European Commission, to the EU High Representative for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy Kaja Kallas, and to the Belgian federal government (CRI, 14 Feb 2025; A-16).
- Process note: the text originated from competing PTB and Ecolo proposals; a global amendment was tabled in commission along a PTB-Ecolo-PS axis; the version brought to the plenary was further reshaped by amendments tabled in session, including new points responding to Trump's 4 February statements (CRI, 14 Feb 2025).
BXL-2425-00013-v13.deep_lectura:
**Analyst read** *(inference — not stated verbatim in the record)*

- **The one hard lever:** almost every ask is addressed upward (federal government, EU, international courts) and is therefore symbolic — except the arms- and dual-use-licensing cancellation, which the Region can in principle execute itself. That single point is where the resolution stops being a position statement and becomes an act with material reach, even if the volume of such licences is contested.
- **What it enables:** by recognising the ICJ's 'plausible risk of genocide' and authorising independent investigators, the text tries to convert a contested characterisation ('genocide') into an administratively endorsed premise that the Region then asks the federal level to act on — agenda-setting through naming.
- **The wedge:** competence and even-handedness. Opponents read a regional parliament legislating foreign policy it cannot execute, on a text they see as marked by one party's framing, as 'importing the conflict'; supporters read Brussels' status as Europe's capital as precisely the reason its voice carries. The in-session amendment blitz (responding to Trump's expulsion plan days earlier) is also a procedural flashpoint, criticised as reshaping the text on the floor.
- **Balancing moves:** the condemnations of Hamas as terrorist and the demand to free hostages function partly to broaden the coalition and pre-empt the 'one-sided' charge — the genuine values split is less about condemning violence than about whether to attach Israel-specific licensing measures and sanctions language.
BXL-2425-00013-v13.raw_fr: La proposition vise à instaurer un cessez-le-feu permanent à Gaza et à activer les leviers propres de la Région : résilier toutes les licences d'exportation ou de transit d'armes et de biens à double usage lorsqu'un usage militaire ne peut être exclu. Elle demande au gouvernement fédéral de réaffirmer son soutien à la procédure devant la Cour internationale de Justice relative aux allégations de génocide à Gaza, de s'opposer à tout déplacement forcé de la population gazaouie et de plaider pour des sanctions contre les responsables, tout en condamnant les actes terroristes du Hamas et en exigeant la libération des otages.

BXL-2425-00013-v14.headline: Call for suspending every military and commercial agreement with Rwanda while it backs the M23 and occupies Congolese territory, demand the immediate withdrawal of Rwandan forces from eastern Congo, and push for asset freezes and EU travel bans on those responsible.
BXL-2425-00013-v14.proposed_by: Les Engagés, MR, Vooruit, Ecolo, PTB, N-VA, cd&v and others (Kazadi, Willocx, Luhahi, Soiresse Njall, Agic, Mandaila, Parga Vega, Busselen, Mouani, Dalle) — ten groups cosigning
BXL-2425-00013-v14.source_brief:
War has gripped eastern Congo for three decades, and in early 2025 the city of Goma fell to the M23 rebels, backed by Rwandan forces. This resolution turns Brussels' diplomatic voice toward the crisis: press international partners to suspend every military or commercial agreement with Rwanda for as long as it supports the M23 and occupies Congolese territory, demand the immediate withdrawal of Rwandan forces, and tighten sanctions — asset freezes abroad and an EU travel ban — on those responsible. It frames the war as driven by a scramble for Congo's minerals and points to a 'double standard' compared with Western sanctions on Russia.

- **The headline demand** — suspend military and commercial cooperation with Rwanda while it backs the M23, and demand Rwandan troops leave Congo.
- **The minerals angle** — back Congo's complaint over the illegal exploitation of its natural resources and the trade in 'blood minerals', the trade the text says fuels the violence.
- **The harder edge** — reinforced sanctions on those backing the M23, including Rwandan leaders: freezing their foreign assets and barring free movement within the EU.
- **The rub:** should a regional parliament push to cut economic and military ties with a foreign state and name its leaders for sanctions — a clear stand against an occupation and a resource war — or does a Brussels resolution reach beyond its powers into federal and EU foreign policy, with the real decisions resting elsewhere?
BXL-2425-00013-v14.deep_facts:
- The resolution concerns the situation in the east of the Democratic Republic of Congo; it was cosigned by ten political groups and examined in commission with its amendments (CRI, 14 Feb 2025; doc A-76).
- Stated objects: international solidarity to condemn the violation of Congo's territorial integrity; to demand the withdrawal of the M23 and Rwandan troops from eastern Congo; to condemn the massacres of civilians, rape used as a weapon of war and exactions of all kinds; and to provide humanitarian aid (CRI, 14 Feb 2025; A-76).
- Operative asks set out by the proposers: a diplomatic and financial engagement of international partners to suspend any military or commercial cooperation agreement with Rwanda, and to demand the immediate withdrawal of Rwandan forces from the DRC; support for Congo's complaint against the illegal exploitation of its natural resources, notably its minerals; reinforcing European coordination to channel humanitarian aid, notably via the Congolese diaspora; immediate deployment of humanitarian assistance for displaced populations; reinforced sanctions against those responsible for the military support to the M23, including Rwandan leaders — freezing their foreign assets and barring free movement within the EU (save for strictly peace-related missions); facilitating fundraising and material collection by the diaspora and Brussels associations (CRI, 14 Feb 2025; A-76).
- Amendments (two, by Mandaila): support the establishment of an international criminal tribunal; study the possibility of asking for the transformation of the UN observation mission (MONUSCO) into an intervention mission; and exhume (resurface) the report of the UN Mapping project (CRI, 14 Feb 2025; A-76).
- Cited human-toll figures (stated, attributed to speakers/UN): at least 10 million lives lost over the conflict's course (a separate figure of more than 6 million dead over three decades was also cited), with millions displaced; more than 400,000 people displaced since the start of 2025; the fall of Goma to the M23 (backed by Rwanda) cited as having caused 3,000 victims, with saturated morgues, overwhelmed hospitals, generalised pillaging including of schools, cut water supply, and bodies recovered from Lake Kivu (CRI, 14 Feb 2025; A-76).
- Cited minerals/financial figures (stated): per a UN group of experts, at least 150 tonnes of coltan illegally exported since April 2024 from the Rubaya mines (cited as among the largest tantalum mines in the world); Rwanda — without a single coltan mine — described as the world's leading exporter of the mineral; the European Commission cited as having signed a memorandum of understanding with Rwanda on raw-material supply, and the EU as having paid €20 million to Rwanda in support of its military operations (CRI, 14 Feb 2025; A-76).
- Context references (not enacted by this text): the strategic airport of Bukavu reported, hours before the session, as having fallen to the M23 and Rwandan troops; regional ceasefire appeals at a summit in Tanzania; the Luanda and Nairobi peace processes and social pacts initiated by the Catholic and Protestant churches of Congo; a European Parliament resolution adopted the previous day on eastern DRC, aimed at suspending the EU–Rwanda partnership on raw materials and calling to halt arms transfers and freeze military assistance to Rwandan forces (CRI, 14 Feb 2025; A-76).
- The proposers stress respect for the competences of the different levels of power and the international legal framework, framing Brussels' role through its status as 'capital of Europe' (CRI, 14 Feb 2025; A-76).
BXL-2425-00013-v14.deep_lectura:
**Analyst read** *(inference — not stated verbatim in the record)*

- **Breadth of sponsorship is the headline fact:** ten groups across the spectrum (from Les Engagés/MR/N-VA to PTB/Ecolo) cosign — signalling a deliberate consensus-symbolism play, partly anchored in Brussels' large Congolese diaspora. The cross-bench buy-in lowers the cost of voting yes and makes abstention, not opposition, the dissenting move.
- **What it enables:** like most regional foreign-policy texts, its asks are addressed upward (federal government, EU, UN) and are not self-executing — its force is agenda-setting and pressure. The most concrete-sounding levers (suspend agreements with Rwanda, freeze assets, EU travel bans, transform MONUSCO) all require federal or EU action the Region cannot itself take.
- **The framing wedge:** the 'two weights, two measures' argument (sanction Russia but not Rwanda) and the 'blood minerals' line tie the war explicitly to European complicity and supply chains — a framing that pushes the text from humanitarian appeal toward an indictment of EU and corporate mineral policy. That framing is where a values split could surface even amid broad agreement on condemning the violence.
- **Timing:** the fall of Bukavu hours before the vote and the European Parliament's resolution the day before gave the text momentum and an external anchor, making a 'Brussels is on the right side of history' framing easy to assert.
BXL-2425-00013-v14.raw_fr: La proposition concerne la situation dans l'est de la République démocratique du Congo. Elle appelle à un engagement diplomatique et financier des partenaires internationaux pour exiger la suspension de tout accord de coopération militaire ou commercial avec le Rwanda tant qu'il soutient le M23 et occupe le territoire congolais, ainsi que le retrait immédiat des forces rwandaises de la RDC. Elle soutient la plainte du Congo contre l'exploitation illégale de ses ressources naturelles, demande le renforcement des sanctions contre les responsables, y compris les dirigeants rwandais (gel des avoirs et interdiction de circuler dans l'Union européenne), et le déploiement d'une aide humanitaire d'urgence.
